title: /respond-html v0.3 — gravity, paths, generator, cleanup
subtitle: v0.3 makes the skill match aesthetics to content, route artifacts into project dirs, regenerate from a Python script, and clean up after itself. React inline on anything that looks wrong.
bluf: v0.3 ships four real changes — (1) gravity tag picks fonts and accent from content type, not random rotation; (2) project-aware output path routes artifacts into ~/dev/SGA/<proj>/.html-answers/ or ~/dev/brain/projects/<area>/.html-answers/ instead of always dumping in ~/dev/personal/; (3) Python generator script at scripts/generate.py is now the canonical path — smoke-test is regenerated, drift can't accumulate; (4) TTL cleanup via /close sweeps 30-day-old artifacts (reactions still attached are exempt). This very page is generated by item 3.

sections.title: Gravity-tag classifier
sections.body:
You said: "case by case is better than rotation." v0.3 replaces the random-rotation logic with a deterministic 8-row mapping from content gravity to font pair + accent.

Gravity tagUse whenAesthetic
sternSecurity audit, contract review, money/legalIBM Plex Serif + Sans, oxford blue
decisiveStrategy proposal, roadmap with clear recommendationCrimson Pro + Manrope, jade
balancedComparison, X vs Y tradeoff analysisSource Serif 4 + Geist, deep teal
distinctiveMockup, design proposal, creative briefFraunces + Bricolage Grotesque, deep violet
editorialRoutine plan, project status, recapNewsreader + Hanken Grotesk, vermilion
measuredAudit (non-security), retro, postmortemEB Garamond + Outfit, amber
lightQuick recommendation, single-decision memoLora + Hanken Grotesk, jade
multidimensionalCompound (data + plan, audit + mockup)Spectral + Manrope, deep violet

This page is gravity decisive (a roadmap with a clear set of recommendations). Hence Crimson Pro + Manrope + jade. The eyebrow at the top says Skill intro · /respond-html v0.3 — future renders will show their gravity tag explicitly there.

Design call

Two roadmap artifacts in a row will both be Crimson Pro + Manrope + jade. That's correct — they're the same shape of artifact. If you want variation within a gravity, that's a v0.4 ask.

sections.title: Project-aware output path
sections.body:
You said: "why /personal? why not brain or SGA?" Right. v0.3 routes artifacts by content:

  1. If pwd is inside ~/dev/SGA/<proj>/, ~/dev/personal/<proj>/, or ~/dev/brain/projects/<area>/ → write to <root>/.html-answers/<slug>/.
  2. Otherwise scan the request for project-name keywords (Reservio, Mandimu, Orkla, etc.) and route accordingly.
  3. Fallback: ~/dev/personal/html-answers/ for cross-cutting / skill-meta content.
Net effect

A plan about Reservio now lands at ~/dev/SGA/reservio/.html-answers/migration-plan/index.html — co-located with the code. The .html-answers/ dir name signals it's auto-managed.

The skill announces the resolved path before rendering. If unclear, it asks via a single AskUserQuestion before writing.

sections.title: Python generator script
sections.body:
Round 3 of /fresh-eyes flagged that the smoke-test had hand-drifted from the template across v0.2.0 → v0.2.2 (BLUF emit order, missing setComment helper, scrollspy var name). v0.3 closes that by making scripts/generate.py the canonical path.

Mechanism: content lives in scripts/smoke-test-content.json. Running python3 scripts/generate.py --content scripts/smoke-test-content.json --out <dir> reads the template, substitutes the {{TOKENS}}, writes index.html. With --pdf, also produces index.pdf via headless Chrome.

# Regenerate the smoke-test
python3 ~/.claude/skills/respond-html/scripts/generate.py \
  --content ~/.claude/skills/respond-html/scripts/smoke-test-content.json \
  --out ~/dev/personal/html-answers/respond-html-intro

# Or with PDF
python3 ~/.claude/skills/respond-html/scripts/generate.py \
  --content content.json --out out/ --pdf
Why a script and not just direct-write?

One source of truth

Template + content are separate. Touch the template once, regen all dependent artifacts.

PDF post-process

Headless Chrome can't easily render a string — it wants a file URL. Generator writes the HTML then prints it.

HTML escaping handled correctly

Title with a & or quotes no longer breaks the page. Generator does it.

Tradeoff

For ad-hoc artifacts (David asks me to plan something), I still write the HTML directly — the generator is an OFFLINE tool for canonical artifacts like this smoke-test. The skill's normal flow doesn't require Python.

sections.title: TTL cleanup via /close
sections.body:
With artifacts spread across many project dirs, manual cleanup gets tedious. v0.3.1 hooks into the /close end-of-session ritual:

  • Sweeps <root>/.html-answers/<slug>/ and ~/dev/personal/html-answers/<slug>/ dirs strictly older than 30 days.
  • Exemption (file-based): a .keep file in the artifact dir pins one slug forever; a .keep in the parent .html-answers/ pins ALL slugs in that project; a feedback.md in the artifact dir pins it (use this when you've exported feedback via 📋 Copy feedback).
  • Find is depth-bounded (-maxdepth 4) and excludes node_modules, .git, .vercel, .next — won't accidentally match a future package literally named html-answers.
  • Silent unless something is swept; trailer echoes the count in /close's Summary step.
Failure mode (honest)

Reactions live in browser localStorage, NOT in the file. The exemption check is purely file-based — it can't detect that you've reacted heavily on an artifact. To preserve reactions across the 30-day TTL, export feedback markdown (📋 Copy feedback button) and save it as <slug>/feedback.md. That's the durable record. If you never exported, your reactions in localStorage are not preserved when the dir is removed.

Practice

If a plan matters past 30 days: (a) touch <slug>/.keep to pin without exporting, OR (b) export feedback via 📋 Copy feedback and save as <slug>/feedback.md — gives you the markdown AND the pin in one move.

sections.title: What v0.3 doesn't do
sections.body:
Six items captured as v0.4-backlog PRDs at ~/dev/brain/projects/respond-html/v0.4-backlog/:

  • 2500+ word artifact handling — sub-pages or scope-down policy when an artifact grows too big.
  • Stats placement — sticky-top vs bottom vs collapsible.
  • Per-reaction-type grouping in markdown copy — group all ❌ first, then 💬, then ✅.
  • Keyboard shortcuts — 1/2/3 keys when a reactable unit is focused.
  • Cross-tab toast on schema mismatch — already partially handled; needs UX polish.
  • Server-side persistence — REJECTED for v0.x with rationale captured.

Each PRD has problem + proposed solution + revisit trigger. /maint-backlog will surface them when relevant.

sections.title: Open questions for you
sections.body:
Things v0.3 didn't fully resolve:

  • Aesthetic list size — 8 gravity rows ship. Want to expand (e.g., add a 9th for "reflective" or "celebratory")?
  • TTL grace — 30 days locked in. Should it be longer for artifacts in brain/projects/ (where you might revisit)?
  • Generator language — Python locked in. If you want Node later (say, when this becomes a web-callable service), the script is small enough to rewrite.
  • Within-gravity variation — currently two decisive plans look identical. v0.4 candidate: optional within-row pair swap so consecutive decisive plans don't feel like a series.

React on this section to flag anything. Defer answers if you'd rather use v0.3 for a bit first.
